wiktionary.gloss: Protected by a covering or shelter.

blocks.etymology: From un- + shamed.

wiktionary.gloss: Not shamed.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English virus, from Latin vīrus (“poison, slime, venom”), via rhotacism from Proto-Italic *weizos, from Proto-Indo-European *wisós (“fluidity, slime, poison”). First use in the computer context by David Gerrold in his 1972 book When HARLIE Was One.

senses.definition: an extremely small living particle that causes disease in people, animals, or plants

examples.en: Wash your hands frequently to avoid spreading the virus.
examples.vi: Hãy rửa tay thường xuyên để tránh làm lây lan vi-rút.

senses.definition: an illness or infection caused by a virus

examples.en: She caught a stomach virus and stayed in bed all day.
examples.vi: Cô ấy bị nhiễm vi-rút đường ruột và nằm liệt giường cả ngày.

senses.definition: a harmful computer program designed to copy itself and damage or destroy data

examples.en: My laptop was infected by a dangerous virus.
examples.vi: Máy tính xách tay của tôi đã bị nhiễm một loại vi-rút nguy hiểm.

thesaurus.definition: (virology) ultramicroscopic infectious agent that replicates itself only within cells of living hosts; many are pathogenic; a piece of nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) wrapped in a thin coat of protein
a harmful or corrupting agency
a software program capable of reproducing itself and usually capable of causing great harm to files or other programs on the same computer

translations.words: vi rút; siêu vi trùng; siêu vi khuẩn; siêu vi; vi trùng; tinh độc

wiktionary.gloss: A submicroscopic, non-cellular structure that consists of a core of DNA or RNA surrounded by a protein coat, that requires a living host cell to replicate, and that sometimes causes disease in the host organism (such agents are often classed as nonliving infectious particles and less often as microorganisms).

examples: Meronym: virion (individual particle)
Some viruses, such as norovirus, cause sporadic outbreaks of gastroenteritis.
wiktionary.gloss: A species thereof.

examples: Under electron microscopy, a few viruses were seen floating near the cells.
wiktionary.gloss: An individual particle thereof: synonym of virion.

examples: Not much virus was detectable on a nucleic acid test; the viral load was very low.
wiktionary.gloss: A quantity of such infectious agents, considered en masse.

examples: He's got a virus and had to stay home from school.
wiktionary.gloss: A disease caused by such an infectious agent; a viral illness.

A type of malware which can covertly transmit itself between computers via networks (especially the Internet) or removable storage such as disks by inserting its code into other executable files, often causing damage to systems and data; also computer virus.
Any type of malware.
Any malicious or dangerous entity that spreads from one place or person to another.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English virus, from Latin vīrus (“poison, slime, venom”), via rhotacism from Proto-Italic *weizos, from Proto-Indo-European *wisós (“fluidity, slime, poison”). First use in the computer context by David Gerrold in his 1972 book When HARLIE Was One.

examples: I'm just going to virus anyone who tries cheating on this game.
wiktionary.gloss: To send or infect an electronic device with a computer virus.

tatoeba.vi: Virus có phải là sinh vật sống không?
Máy tính của Tom đã bị nhiễm virus.

tatoeba.en: The virus will kill everybody on the ship.
tatoeba.vi: Virus sẽ giết chết mọi người trên con tàu.

blocks.etymology: First attested in the 1950s in sense 1, originally in African-American English.

wiktionary.gloss: A person's actions, whether good or bad, will often have consequences for that person.
wiktionary.vi: ác giả ác báo; đời cha ăn mặn, đời con khát nước; gieo nhân nào gặt quả nấy

wiktionary.gloss: Things repeat in cycles.

thesaurus.definition: common North American deer; tail has a white underside

wiktionary.gloss: A medium-sized deer found throughout most of North and Central America and northern portions of South America; Odocoileus virginianus.

blocks.etymology: Clipping of periwig, itself an alteration of French perruque. The meaning of "to reprimand" perhaps came from this being something a bigwig would do or perhaps from the expressions to flip one's wig, wigs on the green, or dash my wig!

senses.definition: An artificial covering of natural or synthetic hair worn on the head.

examples.en: The actor wore a curly blonde wig for the role.
examples.vi: Nam diễn viên đã đội một bộ tóc giả màu vàng xoăn cho vai diễn.

thesaurus.definition: hairpiece covering the head and made of real or synthetic hair
British slang for a scolding

wiktionary.gloss: A head of real or synthetic hair worn on the head to disguise baldness, for cultural or religious reasons, for fashion, or by actors to help them better resemble the character they are portraying.
A bigwig.
An old seal.

blocks.etymology: Clipping of periwig, itself an alteration of French perruque. The meaning of "to reprimand" perhaps came from this being something a bigwig would do or perhaps from the expressions to flip one's wig, wigs on the green, or dash my wig!

senses.definition: To panic, become extremely nervous, or lose emotional control.

examples.en: Don't wig out before the exam has even started.
examples.vi: Đừng hoảng loạn trước cả khi bài thi bắt đầu.

wiktionary.gloss: To put on a wig; to provide with a wig (especially of an actor etc.).
To upbraid, reprimand.

examples: That guy must be high. Look how he's wigging.
wiktionary.gloss: To act in an extremely emotional way; to be overly excited, irritable, nervous, or fearful; behave erratically.
To shoot in the head.

blocks.etymology: Clipping of periwig, itself an alteration of French perruque. The meaning of "to reprimand" perhaps came from this being something a bigwig would do or perhaps from the expressions to flip one's wig, wigs on the green, or dash my wig!

wiktionary.gloss: An expression of shock.

idioms.gloss: To become very angry.
To be shocked or stunned.
To get one's head broken open, typically by someone else as punishment or vengeance.
Synonym of flip one's wig.

phrasal_verbs.gloss: To become extremely emotional or excitable; to lose control of one's emotions.
To understand, perceive or realize (something) that isn't obvious.

tatoeba.en: It'll take you a few weeks to get used to wearing a wig.
tatoeba.vi: Bạn sẽ mất vài tuần để quen với việc đội tóc giả.

wiktionary.gloss: To wolf down; to eat voraciously.
